first: श्रुत्वा धर्मं विजानाति श्रुत्वा त्यजति दुर्मतिम् ।
en: By listening one learns what is right, by listening one gives up bad thinking, by listening one gains knowledge, and by listening one may reach freedom.
Among birds the crow is the lowest, among animals the dog, among holy men the sinner; but the one who speaks ill of others is the lowest of all.
Bronze is cleaned by ash, copper by something sour, a woman by her monthly course, and a river by its flow.
A king who travels is honoured, a Brahmin who travels is honoured, a yogi who travels is honoured, but a woman who wanders is ruined.
One who has money has friends and relatives; he is counted a man in the world, and he is even called learned.
As fate is going to be, so the mind turns, so the effort becomes, and so the helpers appear.

first: कालः पचति भूतानि कालः संहरते प्रजाः ।
en: Time ripens all beings and time destroys them; time is awake while others sleep; truly, time is hard to escape.

first: नैव पश्यति जन्माधः कामान्धो नैव पश्यति ।
en: One born blind cannot see, one blinded by lust cannot see, those drunk with pride cannot see, and one who wants something sees no fault in it.
The soul does its own deeds and enjoys their fruit itself; it wanders through the world by itself and frees itself by itself.

first: राजा राष्ट्रकृतं पापं राज्ञः पापं पुरोहितः ।
en: The king bears the sins of his country, the priest the sins of the king, the husband the sins of his wife, and the teacher the sins of his pupil.
A father in debt is an enemy, so is an unfaithful mother, a beautiful wife, and a son without learning.
Win a greedy person with money, a proud one with folded hands, a fool by going along with him, and a wise one with the truth.
Better no kingdom than a kingdom under a bad king; better no friend than a bad friend; better no pupil than a bad pupil; better no wife than a bad wife.
How can people be happy under a bad king? What comfort comes from a bad friend? What joy is there at home with a bad wife? What fame comes from teaching a bad pupil?
Learn one thing from the lion, one from the crane, four from the rooster, five from the crow, six from the dog, and three from the donkey.
Whatever task a person wants to do, great or small, he should do it with full effort; this one thing is learned from the lion.

first: इन्द्रियाणि च संयम्य वकवत् पण्डितो नरः ।
en: A wise person should control his senses like a crane and, knowing the place, the time and his own strength, carry out all his tasks.
Waking early, being ready to fight, sharing with his kin, and winning his own food by effort: learn these four from the rooster.
Mating in private, storing things from time to time, staying alert, and not trusting easily: learn these five from the crow.
Eating much but being content with little, sleeping deeply yet waking easily, loyalty to the master, and courage: these six are the dog's qualities.

first: सुश्रान्तोऽपि वहेत भारं शीतोष्णं न च पश्यति ।
en: Carrying a load even when very tired, not minding cold or heat, and always going about content: learn these three from the donkey.
A person who practises these twenty qualities will be unbeatable in every kind of work.
